name: Puerto Rico
title: LGBTQ rights in Puerto Rico
extract: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer (LGBTQ) people in Puerto Rico have some of the same protections and rights as non-LGBTQ individuals. Public discussion and debate about sexual orientation and gender identity issues has increased, and some legal changes have been made. Supporters and opponents of legislation protecting the rights of LGBTQ persons can be found in both of the major political parties. Public opposition still exists due, in large part, to the strong influence of the Roman Catholic Church, as well as socially conservative Protestants. Puerto Rico has a great influence on the legal rights of LGBTQ citizens. Same-sex marriage has been legal in the commonwealth since July 2015, after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in the case of Obergefell v. Hodges that same-sex marriage bans are unconstitutional.
